dedupe_keys.name: rasin traffic digital twin for demand management in the hanshin urban area during expo 2025 hanshin expressway and ntt group

description: This field trial used a road traffic digital twin to steer travel demand in the Osaka-Kobe (Hanshin) urban area during the 2025 World Expo in Osaka. Hanshin Expressway and the NTT group, working together since April 2023, built RASiN, a multi-agent traffic simulator covering all expressways and the main arterial roads linked to them, and the Welmos system around it. RASiN forecasts traffic 24 hours a day up to 30 days ahead and reruns a two-hour forecast every 15 minutes on the day, assimilating observed expressway volumes and car probe speeds on ordinary roads; daily origin-destination demand is built from the 2021 road traffic census and ETC 2.0 records with a state-space model and the Fratar method. An earlier NTT DATA interview describes the Kansai traffic twin as built on the agent-based S4 Simulation System with probe data assimilation. From 18 June 2025 the public could use a route search service and the Welmos Agent scheduling app, which compare detours, departure times and public transport by travel time, cost and a social contribution score for travel time, CO2 and crash risk savings; a 30-day congestion forecast calendar was added in September 2025, and the trial was extended to 14 December 2025. Coverage is the Hanshin metropolitan road network. The press releases and a 2025 paper by Hanshin Expressway engineers are free to read online; the twin and data are not public. Outcome: the services ran through and beyond the Expo; forecast accuracy and behaviour change effects were being evaluated, but results were not published in the sources read. The case shows operational traffic management with a data-assimilating agent-based digital twin.
